import ast
import operator

def evaluate_filter(node, user):
    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant):
        return node.value
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Name):
        if node.id in user:
            return user[node.id]
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid field: {node.id}")
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
        left = evaluate_filter(node.left, user)
        # Assuming only one operator for now as per requirements: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=
        # The grammar says expression, which could be complex, let's look at ast.Compare structure
        # node.ops and node.comparators
        # Example: name == 'Ada' -> ops=[Eq()], comparators=[Constant(value='Ada')]
        # Example: id > 1 and email != 'x@y.org' -> This is a BoolOp
        # Wait, ast.Compare can have multiple operators. The prompt says "the comparison operators".
        # Let's keep it simple first.
        op = node.ops[0]
        right = evaluate_filter(node.comparators[0], user)
        
        if isinstance(op, ast.Eq): return left == right
        if isinstance(op, ast.NotEq): return left != right
        if isinstance(op, ast.Lt): return left < right
        if isinstance(op, ast.LtE): return left <= right
        if isinstance(op, ast.Gt): return left > right
        if isinstance(op, ast.GtE): return left >= right
        raise ValueError("Unsupported operator")
    elif isinstance(node, ast.BoolOp):
        values = [evaluate_filter(v, user) for v in node.values]
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.And):
            return all(values)
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Or):
            return any(values)
        raise ValueError("Unsupported boolean operator")
    elif isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Not):
            return not evaluate_filter(node.operand, user)
        raise ValueError("Unsupported unary operator")
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported node type: {type(node)}")

def test():
    user = {"id": 1, "name": "Ada", "email": "ada@example.com"}
    
    # name == 'Ada'
    expr = "name == 'Ada'"
    node = ast.parse(expr, mode='eval').body
    print(f"{expr} -> {evaluate_filter(node, user)}")
    
    # id > 1 and email != 'x@y.org'
    expr = "id > 1 and email != 'x@y.org'"
    node = ast.parse(expr, mode='eval').body
    print(f"{expr} -> {evaluate_filter(node, user)}")

test()
EOF

import ast
def is_safe(expr):
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(expr, mode='eval')
        for node in ast.walk(tree):
            # Allow:
            # ast.Expression (the root)
            # ast.Constant
            # ast.Name
            # ast.Compare
            # ast.BoolOp
            # ast.UnaryOp
            # ast.Not

                # These are necessary for the structure to be traversed:
                ast.Load

        return True
